title: Laughter in the staff room
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on a lunch break in the hospital staff room. A registrar and a consultant from your team are laughing about the appearance of a patient with severe facial burns whom you all saw on the ward round.

A few other staff are in the room, and the door to the corridor is open.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 4 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Laugh along, so as not to stand out in front of seniors.
options.detailed: Laughing along adds to the disrespect and makes it harder to challenge later. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Speak to the registrar privately later about the comments.
options.brief: Less confrontational, but delays addressing it.
options.detailed: A private conversation may feel easier and can still be effective. It ranks second because it doesn't stop the comments now, when they could be overheard.

options.text: Raise it with your educational supervisor.
options.brief: Gets support, though it doesn't address the moment directly.
options.detailed: Your supervisor can help you decide what to do about seniors' behaviour. It ranks third because it doesn't challenge the comments or address them with the people involved.

options.text: Say calmly that the comments don't seem fair to him.
options.brief: A brief, calm challenge in the moment shows respect for the patient.
options.detailed: Comments like these are disrespectful, and could be overheard through the open door. A calm, brief remark addresses it at once without being confrontational. It ranks first, although it is hard to do with seniors.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you challenge disrespectful comments about a patient, even when they come from seniors.
explanation.keyDetails: The comments are about a patient's appearance. The speakers are senior to you. Others could overhear.
explanation.reasoning: [D] challenges calmly in the moment, [B] addresses it privately, and [C] seeks support. [A] endorses the behaviour.
explanation.competing: Some would prefer a private word with the registrar, as it is easier with seniors. The key favours a calm comment now because the remarks could be overheard by others.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 2, treating patients with dignity, including when they aren't present.
